ttl.name: How to Troubleshoot ECU Controlled Systems

item.ptxt: The most difficult case in troubleshooting is when the problem symptom does not occur. In such cases, a thorough customer problem analysis must be carried out, and the problem must be reproduced under the same conditions and environment as when it occurred on the customer's vehicle. If troubleshooting is performed without confirming the problem symptom, important points will be overlooked in the repair work, or misunderstandings will occur, eventually leading to a dead end.

For example, if a problem that occurs when the engine is cold is checked when the engine is hot, or a vibration problem caused by road conditions while driving is checked with the vehicle stopped, the location of the problem can never be identified.

Vibration, heat or water (humidity) intrusion can cause problems that are difficult to reproduce, and the symptom simulation methods introduced here are effective in that they apply external factors to a stopped vehicle.

content5.ptxt: Important Points in the Symptom Simulation Test

In the symptom simulation method, the problem symptom should of course be confirmed, but the range and location of the problem must also be found. To do this, narrow down the circuits that may contain the problem based on the problem symptom before performing the test, and connect a tester in advance. Then, perform the symptom simulation method, judge whether the circuit being tested is abnormal or normal, and confirm the problem symptom at the same time. To narrow down the cause of the problem symptom, refer to the Problem Symptoms Table for each system.

step1.ptxt: Vibration Method: When vibration seems to be the major cause

step3.ptxt: Apply slight vibration, such as tapping lightly by hand, to the parts likely to be the cause, and check whether the malfunction occurs.

atten4.ptxt: Applying strong shock to relays may open their contacts.

step3.ptxt: Gently shake the connector vertically and horizontally.
Gently shake the wire harness vertically and horizontally, and check whether the malfunction occurs.

atten4.ptxt: Pay particular attention to the connector joints, vibration pivot points and body pass-through sections.

step1.ptxt: Heat/Cold Method: When the malfunction seems to occur when cold or hot

step2.ptxt: Using a hair dryer or coolant spray, heat or cool the parts likely to be the cause of the malfunction, and check whether the malfunction occurs.

item.ptxt: When heating, do not exceed +60°C (the temperature at which it can be touched by hand).
Do not open the cover of an ECU, etc. and heat or cool the electronic parts directly.

atten4.ptxt: Coolant spray is available from electronic parts stores.

step1.ptxt: Water Sprinkling Method: When the malfunction seems to occur on a rainy day or in high temperatures

step2.ptxt: Sprinkle water onto the vehicle and check whether the malfunction occurs.

item.ptxt: Do not pour water directly into the engine room; spray a mist onto the front of the radiator to change the temperature and humidity indirectly.
Do not apply water directly to electronic parts.

step1.ptxt: Other: When the malfunction seems to occur when electrical load is excessive

step2.ptxt: Turn on electrical parts such as the heater blower, headlights and rear defogger to increase the electrical load, and check whether the malfunction occurs.
